transcript: I went to go see Pearly Victorious, a non Confederate romp through the Cotton Patch, which is the first play revival of the Broadway season. This play by Ossie Davis was originally produced on Broadway in 1961, and it follows Pearly Victorious Johnson as he returns home to attempt to save the community church, his rural town in Georgia. As the title would suggest, the play takes place post Civil War and is a biting satire on the treatment of black people, especially on plantations, after they were allegedly supposed to be free. There is a very interesting announcement before the start of this play about how this play was originally written in, of course, in the 60s, and how it slowly became a comedy, which I found is very confusing because if you read the original reviews in 1961, they all called it hilarious and biting satire. So I'm not. I'm not sure what they were referring to. And overall, I found this show incredibly enjoyable.
